title: On‑Prem & VPC Maintenance Notice Templates + Terraform Module Primer
body:
Purpose and scope:
This doc collects customer-facing maintenance/upgrade notification templates for Redwood Private (VPC and on-prem), plus an operational primer for Terraform module changes commonly needed during platform upgrades. The intent is a lightweight, editable set of templates field teams can use, and a short ops checklist for running safe upgrades and rollbacks for private customers.

Audience:
- Customer success / account managers (email templates)
- Solutions engineering / field SRE (technical notice & runbook snippets)
- Platform/infra owners (Terraform notes, state migration reminders)

SLA / SLO summary (for use in templates):
- Target availability we advertise: 99.95% monthly for core inference service endpoints (customer contract delivers exact SLA).
- Planned maintenance: exempt from availability SLA for the window if previously communicated per contract terms; we aim to minimize disruptive restarts.
- Severity classifications to include in notices:
  - Maintenance (low risk): rolling restarts, no downtime > 5 minutes per node expected.
  - Service-impacting (medium risk): short interruptions to request routing, brief token errors.
  - Emergency (high risk): immediate mitigation required, possible longer interruptions.

Guiding principles for notices:
- Always state scope (which clusters/regions/customers), exact UTC window, expected impact, and recommended customer action (if any).
- Provide multiple contact channels: account rep, field SRE pager, and support ticket link.
- Give clear rollback criteria: what constitutes abort/rollback vs continue.
- Use consistent placeholders so automation can replace values (e.g., {{customer_name}}, {{cluster_id}}, {{window_start_utc}}, {{expected_duration}}).

Template A — 72‑hour advance notice (standard maintenance)
Subject: Redwood Private maintenance scheduled for {{cluster_id}} — {{window_start_utc}} to {{window_end_utc}} UTC
Hello {{customer_name}} team,

We are writing to let you know of a scheduled maintenance affecting your Redwood Private deployment ({{cluster_id}}) on {{window_date}}. Details: 
- Window: {{window_start_utc}} to {{window_end_utc}} UTC (expected duration: {{expected_duration}})
- Change type: security patch + runtime minor version bump (no config change expected)
- Expected impact: rolling pod restarts; per-node request disruption of up to ~60 seconds; no full-cluster outage expected
- Recommended actions: please avoid scheduling time‑sensitive inference jobs during the window. If you use client-side pinned model versions, confirm compatibility with runtime version {{runtime_version}}.

If your team requires a different window or additional testing, reply to this thread or open a support ticket (link below).

Contacts:
- Account rep: {{account_rep_name}} ({{account_rep_email}})
- Field SRE: {{field_sre}} (pager)
- Support: {{support_ticket_link}}

Thanks,
Redwood Private Operations

Template B — 24‑hour technical heads‑up (more technical audience)
Subject: Technical notice — maintenance on {{cluster_id}} tomorrow {{window_start_utc}} UTC
Hi team,

Quick technical details for the scheduled maintenance: 
- What we will do: apply kernel-level networking patches, restart inference runtime, refresh KV caches, and run health probes.
- Terraform impact: no state changes expected for routine patching; if module variables have a planned change we will state it below.
- Health checks: post-update traffic will be held behind canary routing until 95% of pods pass readiness for 15 minutes.
- Rollback: if >10% of pods fail readiness after 30 minutes, we will roll back to the previous image and open a post-mortem.

Commands we may execute (for field SRE reference):
- kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data node/{{node_name}}
- helm upgrade redwood-runtime --reuse-values --namespace {{ns}} {{chart_ref}} --set image.tag={{new_image_tag}}
- wait-for: curl -sf http://{{pod_ip}}/health || echo FAIL

Template C — Immediate (emergency) notification
Subject: URGENT: Immediate maintenance for {{cluster_id}} — impact possible now
Hi {{customer_name}},

We detected a critical issue affecting request routing to your cluster and are applying an emergency patch now. Impact: requests may see errors (HTTP 5xx) for up to {{expected_duration}}. We will update every 30 minutes until resolved.

Immediate actions for customers: if you have high-priority traffic, switch to your fallback route (if configured) or pause critical jobs until we confirm recovery.

Contact: field-sre@redwood.example.com, support link: {{support_ticket_link}}

Post‑maintenance template (closeout)
Subject: Maintenance completed for {{cluster_id}} — {{window_date}}
Summary: The maintenance window completed at {{completed_at_utc}} UTC. Impact: brief rolling restarts; no data lost; all readiness checks passed.
If you see anomalies, please open a ticket and reference this maintenance window ID {{maintenance_id}}.

Terraform module primer (short ops notes)
Purpose: callouts to include in customer notifications when Terraform changes are part of maintenance (e.g., network/ingress changes, EKS/AKS nodepool updates, or resource renames).

Common change types and recommended messaging snippets:
- Non-state changes (rebuilds, version bumps for images): "This maintenance does not modify your Terraform state. We will only replace runtime images and perform rolling restarts."
- Stateful resource changes (security group changes, VIPs, LB renames): "This maintenance will involve Terraform changes to networking resources. We will provide a pre-signed plan and a short maintenance window for apply. A backup of state will be retained and can be restored on request."

Operational checklist for Terraform-based upgrades (field SRE):
1) Pre-checks:
   - terraform init (in module working dir) and terraform validate
   - terraform plan -out=tfplan -input=false; save plan artifact and share brief summary with customer if state changes are present
   - Verify remote state snapshot exists and S3/GCS bucket retention policy allows rollback snapshot retrieval
2) Apply strategy:
   - Prefer incremental, targeted applies when possible: terraform apply -target=module.network -auto-approve
   - For non-targetable changes, schedule full apply during low traffic window
3) Post-apply validation:
   - Verify nodes/pods register with control plane; run integration smoke tests (sample inference call with known prompt)
   - Confirm load balancer health checks show 100% healthy for 5 continuous minutes
4) Rollback approach:
   - If critical failure: restore state snapshot then terraform apply with restored state or re-run previous known-good plan file
   - Document the last-known-good image tags and tfplan hash in the incident ticket

Terraform change examples to include in customer-facing notes:
- Variable renames: Describe mapping (old_var -> new_var) and whether the change is backward compatible. Example: "We will rename var 'public_subnet_ids' -> 'subnet_ids'. This is a compatibility shim; existing state will keep the old values but we will migrate them during apply; no action required from you."
- Resource replacements: If a resource will be replaced (tainted), indicate expected brief downtime for that component.

Short tf module release checklist (for internal use, can be filtered for customer notes):
- CHANGELOG: one-line summary of user-visible impact
- MIGRATION: brief steps and precise terraform commands to run if manual migration is required
- SMOKE: small CLI test that customer or field SRE can run (curl /health, sample API call)
- ROLLBACK: saved previous tfplan and images with timestamped names in artifact storage

Example customer-facing Terraform paragraph to include in notice:
"This maintenance includes an automated configuration migration of our Terraform modules that manage networking for your cluster. We have created a safe migration plan and snapshot of your Terraform state. No manual action is required unless you manage your own Terraform state; if you do, please reply and we'll coordinate. The apply will be non-destructive for existing resources; any replacement of ephemeral resources will be performed with rolling transitions to avoid disruptions where possible."

Dry-run / staging guidance for customers who want extra assurance:
- Offer a pre-maintenance dry-run: run the same apply in the customer's non-prod project or a staging namespace and share logs.
- Provide a small canary token for customers to run an inference test immediately after maintenance to confirm behavior.

Standard ticket subject template to create when maintenance is scheduled:
"[PD Maintenance] {{customer_name}} {{cluster_id}} — {{window_date}} — {{maintenance_id}}"
Ticket body should include: planned commands, tfplan link, S3/GCS snapshot id, rollback criteria, on-call roster, and post-mortem owner.

Runbook excerpt for post‑maintenance verification (short list):
- Check 1: kubectl get pods -n {{ns}} | grep -v Running
- Check 2: curl -sS -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" https://{{customer_endpoint}}/v1/health -> expect 200
- Check 3: review tracing for 30 minutes, look for error spike > 2x baseline

Customer opt-out and blackout windows:
- Document any customer-requested blackout windows (no maintenance) in the ticket and escalate to product for exceptions to global rollout schedules.

Templates for short Slack/Teams updates (channel to customer or internal):
- Pre-window internal: "PD maintenance for {{cluster_id}} starting {{window_start_utc}}UTC — rolling updates, canary traffic only until green. Field SRE: {{field_sre}}."
- Live update: "Applying patch to {{cluster_id}} — step {{step_number}}/{{total_steps}} complete. Current impact: {{current_impact}}."
- Complete: "Maintenance finished: {{cluster_id}} — completed at {{completed_at_utc}}UTC. Post-checks OK. Ticket: {{ticket_link}}."

Notes on documentation and auditable artifacts:
- Always attach the terraform plan file and a state snapshot id to the maintenance ticket.
- Keep an artifact of the exact container image tags used in the upgrade and the helm chart hash.

Open questions / TODOs for this doc:
- Add a short checklist for customers that self-host their TF state (step-by-step for preflight snapshot and restore).
- Create a one-click email generator in the console to replace placeholders and schedule outbound notices.

Appendix: minimal sample email (copy-paste friendly)
Subject: Redwood Private — Scheduled maintenance for {{cluster_id}} on {{window_date}}
Hello {{customer_name}} team,

We will perform scheduled maintenance on your cluster ({{cluster_id}}) starting {{window_start_utc}} UTC. Expected duration: {{expected_duration}}. Impact: rolling restarts with transient request errors possible per node during restart. We will perform canary validation and rollback if health checks fail.

No action required unless you manage Terraform state yourself; if so, reply and we will coordinate.

Thank you,
Redwood Private Operations

-- end of doc --
